body:
Reply with plain text only, no JSON, no preamble, and do not send messages to anyone else. Do not ask questions; decide.

You are drafting short Narrator lines for a Halloween D&D video game, "The Crooked Moon". The Narrator is the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of a ghost train, telling the tale afterwards in a folksy Southern drawl. This batch is set in the Crooked House, a haunted manor on a hill above the village of Wickermoor: a house that warps itself, built on old dark power. A storm has shut the party inside. Here the Vagrant's humour is gone. He is hushed, dry and dead level, the drawl stripped down to bare bones, with silences in it. Never a joke, never a gloat; the dead are respected.

Rules every line follows:
- Second person ("you"), present tense. Never use any name, never the word {name}; the line is for whoever walks up, any hero.
- One or two sentences, under about 30 words in all. The second sentence is usually the turn or the payoff.
- Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a temperature) over adjectives. No game words (no HP, roll, check, level, search, DC, saving throw, class names). Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No modern slang. No winks at the player.
- No facts the party has not earned: only what a person standing in front of the thing could see, smell, hear or touch. Use only the facts given for each key; do not invent new people, places, monsters, props, objects or history. Do not name any real-world place.
- Drop a final g ("hangin'", "creakin'") in about one line in three, not more, and use no other dialect spelling (reckon, ain't and folks are fine, sparingly). The fiddle is never written or mentioned.
- Plain punctuation only: commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, quotation marks. No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no backticks, no stage directions, no placeholders other than where a key below says an EXTRA line may use {name}.
- Do not repeat an image in neighbouring keys. The house's palette, to spread across the lines, one or two details per line, not all at once: sepia rot and mildew green, faded rose and teal wallpaper, bruised purple upholstery, cracked tile, cobweb grey, dust and mildew; nothing square (doors that are trapezoids, frames that lean, floors that slope, a bulging turret); weasels scratching inside every wall; teeth clicking underfoot; a clock ticking somewhere; the storm; windows sealed and black, streaked with rain, lit by lightning. Sweet rot is the smell of the dining room only, burnt flesh the smell of the kitchen only, copper the smell of the bathroom only. The rooms are unlit unless the party brings light.

Output format, nothing else: for each key, a block exactly like

KEY enter:h2_foyer
PLAIN: the line
PLAIN2: a second plain line (only when the key says so)
EXTRA [class:bard]: the extra line (only when the key says so; this one may begin with {name} and say what that hero does or notices; it must still make sense alone)

Every key needs its PLAIN line, which must stand alone for any hero.
BATCH D: THE RETRY LINES. When the whole party falls in a fight in the Crooked House, the Vagrant stops his own telling, puts the party back on its feet and starts the fight again from where they entered that floor. This is the Vagrant interrupting himself, quietly, in this house's hushed, dry, dead-level voice: no joke, no scolding, no gloating, not harsh and not cheerful. Warm underneath, steady. Each line says, in the story's own terms, that the tale did not end there and that he will tell that part over. Never use the words retry, restart, game, save, again-and-again, dead, die, defeat or lose. Do not describe the fall itself. Each line is the same kind of thing as: "Now wait just a minute, friends, that isn't how this part goes. Let me back the song up to where you stepped in." Do not copy that wording; vary every line.

For each key give PLAIN and PLAIN2 (two different plain lines), each one or two sentences, under about 28 words. Each line may mention the fight's own thing in a few words (the stone bird, the tune, the table, the chiming clock, the shadow in the nursery cupboard and so on) but must not name a monster. Where the key says how the party comes back, work that in once or twice across the whole batch, not in every line.

KEY defeat:crooked_house (general; the fallback for any fight in the house, so it must fit anywhere; give PLAIN, PLAIN2 and PLAIN3)
KEY defeat:ch_peacock (first floor, the white marble peacock in the gallery; the party comes back at the front door)
KEY defeat:ch_dance (first floor, the tune on the dance floor in the music room; back at the front door)
KEY defeat:ch_feast (first floor, the feast on the dining table; back at the front door)
KEY defeat:ch_petunia (first floor, the woman in black in the conservatory; back at the front door)
KEY defeat:ch_clock (second floor, the chiming grandfather clock; back at the top of the stair)
KEY defeat:ch_lurker (second floor, the children's room and the dark in it; back at the top of the stair)
KEY defeat:ch_bath (second floor, the bathroom and the rising red water; back at the top of the stair)
KEY defeat:ch_jasper (second floor, the master bedroom and the heaving bed; back at the top of the stair)
KEY defeat:ch_quasits (third floor, the nursery and the toys; back at the top of the stair)
KEY defeat:ch_wisp (third floor, the library and the grey cat; back at the top of the stair)
KEY defeat:ch_bogle_curse (anywhere in the house; something that bursts from a crack in the plaster; the party stays where they stand)
KEY defeat:ch_roar (third floor, the trophy room and the roar in the ceiling; back at the top of the stair)
KEY defeat:ch_vessla (the attic, the cauldron room, the last fight of the house; back at the foot of the ladder up from the trophy room)
result:
KEY defeat:crooked_house
PLAIN: Hold on now, I am tellin' this crooked. You still have breath in the dark, and the rain is still beating the sealed glass.
PLAIN2: No, my tongue slipped in the dust and mildew. Let me draw a breath and take you back a few steps along the sloping boards.
PLAIN3: That ain't the way your thread runs out in these walls. Let me set the lantern down and tell this stretch from where you stood.

KEY defeat:ch_peacock
PLAIN: Wait now, the white marble bird does not finish the tale here. You are standing inside the front door, with the storm sealed behind you.
PLAIN2: I told that gallery turn wrong. Let me take it back before the stone feathers ever stirred in the sepia dark.

KEY defeat:ch_dance
PLAIN: Hold there, the tune on the dance floor ain't the last sound you hear. Let me hush that melody and start the verse over.
PLAIN2: That measure went sour in my mouth. You are still on your feet, before the music room floor ever caught your boot.

KEY defeat:ch_feast
PLAIN: No, the smell of sweet rot at that table does not close your story. Let me clear the telling and walk you in fresh.
PLAIN2: I got ahead of myself by the long dining table. Let us step back before you ever reached for a chair.

KEY defeat:ch_petunia
PLAIN: Easy now, the woman in black among the wet glass did not end your night. Let me tell it from the threshold, steady and plain.
PLAIN2: That ain't how the conservatory goes down in my memory. Let me back my voice up while the lightning still shows you standing.

KEY defeat:ch_clock
PLAIN: Hold a second, the chiming grandfather clock struck out of turn in my head. Let me wind the hands back to the top of the stair.
PLAIN2: No, the brass pendulum does not cut your thread short. Let me tell this landing over before the case ever chimed.

KEY defeat:ch_lurker
PLAIN: Wait now, the dark in the children's room ain't where you stay. Let me bring the light back to the doorway and tell it right.
PLAIN2: I let the shadow in that small room swallow my words. You are still standing outside the leaning frame, breathing cold air.

KEY defeat:ch_bath
PLAIN: No, the rising red water and the smell of copper do not take you down. Let me drain that telling and start from dry cracked tile.
PLAIN2: I spoke that wrong, friends. Let us step back from the basin before the red water ever climbed the porcelain.

KEY defeat:ch_jasper
PLAIN: Hold on, the heaving bed in the master room ain't the end of the road. Let me smooth the telling out from the hall.
PLAIN2: That part came out twisted, like the doorframe by the bruised purple upholstery. Let me take the tale back before the bedposts shook.

KEY defeat:ch_quasits
PLAIN: Wait now, the nursery and its scattered toys do not finish your walk. Let me gather the thread back under the cobweb grey.
PLAIN2: No, I reckon I told that nursery corner too quick. Let me set you back on the third-floor landing before a single toy moved.

KEY defeat:ch_wisp
PLAIN: Hold there, the grey cat among the dusty shelves ain't the last thing you see. Let me turn the page back and read it true.
PLAIN2: My voice wandered in the dark of the library. Let me bring you back before those quiet paws ever crossed the floorboards.

KEY defeat:ch_bogle_curse
PLAIN: Easy now, what burst from the crack in the plaster does not end the night. You are still standing right where your boots were planted.
PLAIN2: No, the weasels scratchin' behind the faded rose and teal paper heard a different turn. Stay where you stand while I tell that breath over.

KEY defeat:ch_roar
PLAIN: Wait a moment, the roar in the trophy room ceiling ain't what brings the roof down on this tale. Let me steady my voice and start again.
PLAIN2: I let that sound overhead rattle the telling. Let me take you back before the dust shook loose from the beams.

KEY defeat:ch_vessla
PLAIN: No, friends, the cauldron room up in the attic is not where your story goes cold. You have your hands on the ladder rungs down in the trophy room.
PLAIN2: Hold on now, the last room under the crooked roof ain't finished with you yet. Let me drop my voice and tell the climb one more time.
